text:
maya: heads up — trying to run the new js sdk sample in Cloudflare Workers and it immediately crashes on import. stack shows "Buffer is not defined" and some package export resolution errors. anyone seen this?

alex: yep, CF Workers is a webworker env — no Buffer, no fs, no process. you need an edge-friendly build (esbuild/vite target webworker or rollup with output.format="es"). also make sure the SDK bundle doesn't pull in node-only deps.

maya: i tried bundling with esbuild + external: ["node-fetch"] but still failing. wrangler publish fails with: "Module has unsupported or experimental syntax" referencing package exports.

sam: are you using "type": "module" in package.json? and check package exports in upstream deps — sometimes packages ship dual ESM/CJS and the worker bundler picks the wrong entry. we had to add a small shim to force the ESM entry in our sample.

maya: what's the shim look like?

alex: simplest is an import alias file. e.g. create src/edge-entry.mjs:
```
// edge-entry.mjs
export { default as Redwood } from 'some-sdk/dist/edge/index.mjs';
```
then import from './edge-entry.mjs' in worker. avoids resolving to node CJS entry.

sam: also watch out for webcrypto differences — Node's crypto.randomUUID / createHash vs SubtleCrypto. our SDK uses node crypto for signing in server builds; for workers we swap to crypto.subtle + subtle-friendly helpers. sample app needs that runtime branch.

maya: ok that helps. another thing: miniflare local run kept failing with "crypto.subtle is undefined" even though i have miniflare@2.0 — any config?

alex: miniflare historically didn't polyfill subtle fully. upgrade to miniflare@2.3+ and enable the --compat flag, or use the wrangler dev (which sets a better runtime). if you need to test subtle, there's an env var we added in the sample: MINIFLARE_WEB_CRYPTO=1 in the README.

maya: notes on TypeScript: tsserver marks imports from 'some-sdk' as "cannot find module" unless i add "dom" or "webworker" to tsconfig.lib. current sample tsconfig has lib ["es2020"] only.

kelly: yeah add "lib": ["es2021", "webworker"] and set "moduleResolution": "bundler" or "node16" depending on toolchain. also set types to [] to avoid node types bleeding in.

sam: for CI, we should run a quick smoke test with miniflare and also esbuild build step that targets webworker. build-bot can add a matrix job: { node: 18, bundler: esbuild, miniflare: latest } and fail the sample if it bundles node-only deps.

build-bot: created draft pipeline job devex/sample-edge-ci #745, will post link when ready.

maya: one last pain: Wrangler throws "experimentalModules" warnings and local prod sesh differs from cloud. any recommended wrangler config?

alex: set "compatibility_date" to a recent date, set "main": "./dist/worker.mjs" and ensure bundler output is ESM, and add "modules: true" in wrangler.toml. avoid using commonjs shims.

kelly: action items: 1) update sample README with esbuild config snippet + MINIFLARE env note, 2) add tsconfig webworker example, 3) add CI smoke job. i'll own the README + TS changes.

maya: thanks — will try the edge-entry shim and report back. :thumbsup:

devex-bot: linked resources: https://github.com/cloudflare/workers-docs-compat, https://esbuild.github.io/api/#format, https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/234 (edge-compat notes).

maya: marking this thread solved for now, will re-open if anything else crops up.
